name: Shopware
title: Shopware SvelteKit Storefront — Svelte Commerce Connector
description: Svelte Commerce on Shopware’s Store API: 28 of 43 services wired, with cart, checkout and sign-in; coupons are the gap. Setup, environment and fixes.
lede: Shopware’s Store API is one of the cleanest headless surfaces of the 26. The connector carries the cart and the customer’s session in the `sw-context-token` header, captured and replayed like a cookie.
verdict: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired; coupons are the one recorded gap. The connector found Store API routes to apply and remove a promotion code on a cart, but none to list or validate a code on its own.

quickStart.text: one connector at a time: remove the two the storefront ships with, add this one
point it at your Shopware shop

quickStartNote: The guide removes only `@misiki/litekart-connector`. A fresh clone’s `package.json` also lists `@misiki/vendure-connector`, and with two connectors installed and neither of them Litekart’s, the build stops and asks for `PUBLIC_CONNECTOR` — so this removes both.

env.name: PUBLIC_SHOPWARE_API_URL
env.note: Your Shopware shop’s URL; the connector calls its Store API. Boot fails, naming this variable, if it is missing.

env.name: PUBLIC_SHOPWARE_ACCESS_KEY
env.note: The sales channel’s access key, sent as `sw-access-key`. It chooses the sales channel and is meant for storefront use. If it is unset, `PUBLIC_SHOPWARE_API_KEY` or `PUBLIC_SHOPWARE_ACCESS_TOKEN` is read in its place.

env.name: PUBLIC_CONNECTOR
env.note: Only when more than one connector is installed: `@misiki/shopware-connector` names the one this build runs on.

envNote: `init.ts` hands the connector every `PUBLIC_SHOPWARE_*` variable that is set, camel-cased. The guide also lists `PUBLIC_SHOPWARE_API_SECRET`, `PUBLIC_SHOPWARE_STORE_ID` and `PUBLIC_SHOPWARE_CHANNEL_ID`; the connector’s source does not read them — the sales channel is chosen by the access key alone.
backendSettings: Use a sales channel’s access key: the Store API chooses the sales channel by the `sw-access-key` header, and there is no route that picks a store by ID.
Let the storefront’s origin make cross-origin requests to Shopware (CORS): in production the browser calls `PUBLIC_SHOPWARE_API_URL` directly, not only the server.
howItWorks: The connector speaks Shopware’s Store API, the shopper-facing half of Shopware’s API. Every request carries the sales channel’s `sw-access-key`; the cart and the signed-in customer live in the `sw-context-token` header, which the connector captures from responses and replays like a cookie.

Installing the package is the whole switch. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever `@misiki/*-connector` is installed, and `src/lib/core/connectors/init.ts` hands it every `PUBLIC_SHOPWARE_*` variable that is set, camel-cased, at boot — in the server hook for server rendering and in the client hook for the browser, which must reach the same URL in production.

There is no Litekart API behind the storefront here, so store identity — name, logo, currency, menus, plugin toggles, theme colours — comes from `src/lib/core/connectors/default-store.json` merged under the default export of `kitcommerce.config.ts`. Until you override it, the store is called “Test”. Any Litekart REST path the connector still inherits is answered from that local data, or resolved empty, rather than requested.
limitations: Coupons: not wired — the connector found Store API routes to apply and remove a promotion code on a cart, but none to list or validate a code on its own.
Pages that depend on a service that is not wired render their empty state rather than failing.
Homepage sections other than the live product list come from the active theme’s static content — the standing rule for themes.
The Conversational Shopping assistant is Litekart-only; its widget stays hidden when another connector is active.

troubleshooting.problem: Boot fails with “the shopware connector is active but PUBLIC_SHOPWARE_API_URL is not set”
troubleshooting.fix: Add `PUBLIC_SHOPWARE_API_URL` to `.env`. A production Node build and Docker read `PUBLIC_*` from the process environment rather than `.env`, so set it on your deploy platform too.

troubleshooting.problem: The build stops with “Several commerce connectors are installed … Set PUBLIC_CONNECTOR to pick one”
troubleshooting.fix: More than one `@misiki/*-connector` is in `package.json` and none is Litekart’s. Uninstall the ones you do not run — a fresh clone also lists `@misiki/vendure-connector` — or set `PUBLIC_CONNECTOR='@misiki/shopware-connector'`.

troubleshooting.problem: Boot fails with “PUBLIC_…_API_URL is set, but it configures a different backend than the one this build runs on”
troubleshooting.fix: Another backend’s variable is still set, usually left over from the one you switched from. Remove it, or install that backend’s connector. `PUBLIC_LITEKART_API_URL` is exempt: it only points the dev proxy.

troubleshooting.problem: The store is called “Test”, or shows the wrong name and logo
troubleshooting.fix: Store identity is static on this backend. Set `name`, `logo`, `currencyCode` and the rest in the default export of `kitcommerce.config.ts`; `src/lib/core/connectors/default-store.json` lists every field.

troubleshooting.problem: `[shopware] no native implementation for get /api/...` in the console
troubleshooting.fix: The connector’s REST guard caught a path inherited from Litekart and answered it empty instead of requesting it. Each path is reported once. Harmless if Shopware has no such feature; if it has one, the fix belongs in the connector’s matching service.

troubleshooting.problem: `http proxy error: api/... ECONNREFUSED` in dev
troubleshooting.fix: A Litekart REST path was requested from outside the connector, so its guard never saw it. Vite proxies `/api` to `PUBLIC_LITEKART_API_URL`, or to `localhost:7000`.

`@misiki/kitcommerce-core` declares it as a peer, and `vite.config.ts` redirects that specifier to whichever connector is installed. Make sure exactly one `@misiki/*-connector` is listed in `package.json`.

faq.q: Can I run a Shopware store on Svelte Commerce today?
faq.a: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired against Shopware’s Store API, and coupons are the only recorded gap. Like every connector, it has not been run against a live production Shopware store.

faq.q: How do I switch Svelte Commerce to Shopware?
faq.a: Remove the connectors the storefront ships with, install `@misiki/shopware-connector`, set `PUBLIC_SHOPWARE_API_URL` in `.env` and start the dev server. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever connector is installed, so no file in the storefront changes.

faq.q: How does the cart keep its session on Shopware?
faq.a: Through the `sw-context-token` header. Shopware returns it with the cart and the customer session; the connector captures it and sends it back on later requests, the way a browser replays a cookie.

faq.q: Has the Shopware connector been run against a real Shopware store?
faq.a: Not against a live production instance — no Svelte Commerce connector has been. It was written by reading Shopware’s authoritative API source, and the Svelte Commerce maintainers ask Shopware’s own maintainers for a sandbox to run it against.

openQuestion: Is there a Store API route for promotion or voucher lookup — not just applying one to a cart? The connector found apply and remove, but no way to list or validate a code on its own.
